From June 1 on, he hit a staggering .113/.223/.186 in 49 games- a wRC+ of 10- leading to him being placed on the Developmental List from mid-August until September. He recovered a bit in September, but there are no two ways around it: this was a disastrous season for Clifford. Complicating matters further, there were some fairly high expectations of him in more than a few circles- with Pete Alonso not being re-signed and Clifford knocking on the door, the possibility was there that the slugger could play his way into a role at some point in 2026. Those two independent storylines merged in quite possibly one of, if not the, biggest Mets minor league disappointments of the 2026 season. He missed almost four months due to an oblique injury, and in the games that he pitched prior to being placed on the injured list and after being activated from it, he wasn’t good either. Because of the injury, it’s hard to evaluate whether or not the right-hander was overmatched against Double-A hitters, or if he was pitching compromised because of it. Either way, 2026 was a lost year for him and he is hopefully fully healthy and ready to go in April 2026. His fastball doesn’t really have the best shape and is more of a set-up pitch than a strikeout pitch, but it certainly did its job and effectively set-up his changeup, which was a true plus pitch in 2026, limiting batters to a .175/.245/.299 batting line with a 47.6% Whiff Rate. Outside of that fastball-changeup combination though, Wenninger really had nothing. Batters hit .293/.378/.509 against his sliders; his sweeping slider (.152/.263/.273) was quite a bit better than his gyro slider (.349/.423/.602), but was used a fraction of the amount (23.3% to 8.9%). Further complicating everything was that the right-hander, who came into the season known as a pitcher with good command and control, had trouble against the more experienced Triple-A hitters who also had the ABS system on their side, and his walk rate suffered. There’s still potential in Wenninger, but the right-hander still feels like he is a change or two away from being a potential major league contributor. When he was promoted to Binghamton, almost overnight, Voit became one of, if not the, most exciting players in the minor league system. In 29 games with the Rumble Ponies, he posted a wRC+ of 158- and that takes into account a little lull that he had in September; remove those 7 games, and he had a 202 wRC+ against Eastern League pitchers. Early on in the season, Voit began working with his hitting coaches to refine his decisions at the plate and to focus on swinging at good pitches and making good contact, putting extra effort into studying scouting reports and figuring out how to get pitchers to work to his strengths rather than him falling into their pitching traps. By the time the summer began, he was doing just that, and the results spoke for themselves. Some of the underlying metrics propping up his numbers are unsustainable- no player in major league history since LD% began being tracked has ever posted a 30% LD% and a BABIP over .400- so expect some likely regression in 2027, but if the infielder can continue producing even a fraction of the number he produced during the dog days of the summer, that’s money. April: 4 G (4 GS), 17.1 IP, 13 H, 12 R, 11 ER (5.71 ERA), 11 BB, 26 K, .364 BABIP (Double-A) May: 6 G (6 GS), 28.2 IP, 25 H, 13 R, 11 ER (3.45 ERA), 11 BB, 32 K, .323 BABIP (Double-A) June: 5 G (5 GS), 22.0 IP, 16 H, 8 R, 7 ER (2.86 ERA), 13 BB, 25 K, .273 BABIP (Double-A) July: 4 G (4 GS), 22.2 IP, 14 H, 9 R, 7 ER (2.78 ERA), 10 BB, 37 K, .341 BABIP (Double-A) August: 5 G (5 GS), 19.0 IP, 21 H, 16 R, 14 ER (6.63 ERA), 17 BB, 25 K, .388 BABIP (Triple-A) September: 3 G (3 GS), 15.1 IP, 13 H, 7 R, 6 ER (3.52 ERA), 4 BB, 18 K, .257 BABIP (Triple-A) 2026 Season: 19 G (19 GS), 90.2 IP, 68 H, 42 R, 36 ER (3.57 ERA), 45 BB, 120 K, .314 BABIP (Double-A) / 8 G (8 GS), 34.1 IP, 34 H, 23 R, 20 ER (5.24 ERA), 21 BB, 43 K, .337 BABIP (Triple-A) Jonathan Santucci threw 50.0 strong innings in Double-A Binghamton last season, posting a 2.52 ERA in 10 starts with 33 hits allowed, 18 walks, and 63 strikeouts, and he followed that up by throwing another 90.2 strong innings with the Rumble Ponies between April and August. When the southpaw was promoted to Triple-A Syracuse, things went poorly at first, but by the time the end of the season rolled around, he righted the ship to a degree; In his first four Triple-A starts, he allowed 12 earned runs in 14.0 innings, allowing 16 hits, walking 16, and striking out 18 and in his final four Triple-A starts, he allowed 8 earned runs in 20.1 innings, allowing 18 hits, walking 5, and striking out 25. The left-hander corrected his atrocious walk rate, but in throwing more pitches in the zone, let himself get hurt by the long ball; his home run rate spiked, allowing 5 home runs in those 20.1 innings, as opposed to 1 over the course of his first four starts, and 4 over the course of all 90.2 innings he pitched in Binghamton. I think that encapsulates Santucci as a pitcher- he is most effective when pitching around the zone and getting batters to get themselves out rather than dominating them in it, so it will be interesting to see how he fares in a larger Triple-A sample size next season. For other stretches, he looked like a star, spraying the ball around the field and pulling fly balls for homers. The AMD all-stock acquisition fits a now-familiar pattern in semis of paying in equity for AI-adjacent capability rather than cash, a structure that has historically been read as dilutive at the margin but signalling strategic urgency; all-stock deals of this size in this space have tended to pressure the acquirer on announcement while the strategic case is litigated over the following quarters, with integration risk in research-led targets the usual point of failure. The Goldman succession story is the standard board-process leak: comparable episodes at large banks have historically been non-events for the franchise unless the timeline hardens or the transition becomes contested, and the company's characterisation of discussions as routine is the standard response. On the eve of its 10-year anniversary, Rancho Santa Fe restaurant Nick & G’s will be undergoing a complete renovation and menu refresh. The eatery will close in mid-October and reopen with a brand new look in November. The update will include a redesigned indoor dining room and bar, and new private event and patio spaces. A California-Italian-inspired menu will feature handmade pastas, pizzas and seasonal shared plates. The Lilian Rice building at the corner of Paseo Delicias and La Granada has a long history, originally built in the 1920s and serving as the home of the Millar family, one of the earliest Rancho Santa Fe families. It was previously Delicias restaurant for 24 years and briefly Ponsaty’s. Local resident Sandra DiCicco-Bonar of the Grand Restaurant Group took over and opened Nick & G’s in 2017, naming it after her children Nicolas and Gianina. “As we approach our 10th anniversary, we wanted to honor what our guests have always loved about Nick & G’s while creating something fresh for the next chapter, said Gianina Pickens, the “G” of Nick and G’s, and chief operating officer of Grand Restaurant Group. ”It’s incredibly meaningful to continue our family’s hospitality legacy in a place that has become such a special part of the Rancho Santa Fe community.” Leading the restaurant group, Pickens is carrying on her family’s culinary heritage that goes back to her grandfather Nicola DiCicco, who emigrated from Pacentro, Italy, and built a family restaurant business with his four brothers starting in the Fresno area, according to a news release. Chef/Partner Alex Carballo has joined Pickens in the renovation effort. Carballo has been with the Grand Restaurant Group for about a year, bringing a resume that spans 20 years in the local San Diego hospitality scene, including stops at Stone Brewing World Bistro & Gardens and Fox Point Farms—he was also the chef at The Crosby Club when it first opened. In addition to Nick & G’s, Carballo is also overseeing the Grand Restaurant Group’s newly reimagined Nómada in Carlsbad and recently announced Bangers BBQ, set to open next year in Escondido. In Rancho Santa Fe Carballo is working to bring his vision to life, with his hands on everything from tinkering with the menu to picking plants for the patio. He understands his mission to deliver  a high-quality dining experience, “meeting the high expectations that this community does have.” Carballo’s design inspiration was developed in consultation with Rachael Lorraine Harris and Michael Soriano. The look will invoke the energy of the Amalfi Coast, brighter, lighter and more contemporary, bringing in very different shades of yellow, orange and blue with lots of greenery and nature-inspired patterns. A grandiose olive tree will take root at the center of the dining room, which will feature all-new custom-made banquettes and tables. Guests will be able to see through to the updated, lightened-up bar and lounge through a beautiful new wine cellar. They will also be able to see into the kitchen. “You should feel like you’re taken away someplace else,” Carballo said of his vision. “In Rancho Santa Fe you already get that amongst the trees and beautiful Spanish architecture… to enter the restaurant you will see and feel the difference, feel the warmth and nature.” They hope to create a “wow” vibe inside, but they also hope the outdoor spaces will be places people will want to spend some time. The patio will be lush with plants with a new wave shade canopy overhead, and the courtyard in the back will have a garden feel with more greenery and water features. Carballo is still crafting the new menu—some Nick & G’s favorites will remain, but the update will focus on coastal Italian-Americana dishes, a smaller and fine-tuned menu showcasing the best local produce, handmade pasta and seafood. He will spend the downtime during construction working on wine pairing, hiring new people, training on service and learning the menu. Having started out years ago in Rancho Santa Fe, Carballo is part of a close-knit family of local chefs that includes people such as Johnny Freyberg at The Crosby and Patrick Ponsaty at The Inn. Nick & G’s has continued to build relationships and collaborate with the Rancho Santa Fe community—they recently teamed up to host an exclusive multi-course Patrimony Estate wine dinner. Nick & G’s hopes to continue offering experiences like that with live music, special dinners and community events. Carballo is excited by the village revitalization that now includes several different dining options such as Paseo and the newly opened Paseo Pizza & Gelato, the new Rancho Sandwich and Creamery, the mainstay of Mille Fleurs, Lilian’s and the cafe at The Inn and spots like Thyme in the Ranch, Caffe Positano and Rancho Roasters. And coming soon, a new Nick & G’s. “I like the energy when there’s more…it gives people a little more variety and a reason to go into Rancho Santa Fe, and we’re in the heart of it,” Carballo said. “I’m glad that the family and partners are trusting me to take this and show the community we’re here to stay and give them something new and great to look forward to.” For updates ahead of the reopening, follow along at nickandgs.com and @nickandgs on Instagram. title: Wide Open GS Title Battle Entering Road Atlanta Finale - Sportscar365
content: Forty-five cars set for Friday’s season-ending Fox Factory 120 at Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta… Under the current IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge points structure introduced in 2021, there’s been an 80 percent hit rate of drivers leading the points at the second-to-last race and securing the championship at the Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta season finale. The two times out of ten it didn’t happen, the lead was 30 points or less. First-time 2026 GS championship leaders Austin Krainz and Stevan McAleer in the No. 27 AutoTechnic Racing BMW M4 GT4 EVO come to the Fox Factory 120 with a lead of exactly 30 points. Krainz and McAleer haven’t won but have been the model of consistency for two years straight. They can only clinch outright with a win; otherwise, they’ll need to finish ahead of their rivals. This year, they’ve finished between second and 11th in eight of nine races, and only have a worst result of 17th. They’re the fifth different GS entry to lead the championship this year, following the No. 71 Rebel Rock Racing Aston Martin Vantage GT4 Evo, No. 57 Winward Racing Mercedes-AMG GT GT4, No. 95 Turner Motorsport BMW M4 GT4 EVO and No. 13 McCumbee McAleer Racing Ford Mustang GT4. Emblematic of the topsy-turvy nature of 2026, Krainz and McAleer’s pre-Michelin Raceway point total of 2,190 points is the lowest entering the final round by any GS leader since the current points system was introduced. They’re ahead of the aforementioned No. 95 Turner BMW featuring past GS champions Dillon Machavern (2017) and Luca Mars (2025) by 30 points and Robert Noaker in the No. 13 MMR Ford by 40. Both Turner and MMR have second entries this race, including MMR’s debuting No. 61 Ford Mustang GT4 of Jenson Altzman and Erik Evans. Fourth-placed Michael Cooper and Moisey Uretsky (120 back, No. 44 Ibiza Farm Motorsport McLaren Artura GT4) and fifth-placed Bryce Ward (130 back, No. 57 Winward Mercedes-AMG) are in with a mathematical shot. Cooper and Uretsky won both at Indianapolis last race and Michelin Raceway last year. Wild point swings can occur with up to a maximum 340-point swing between first (350 points) and 30th (10). The only GS second-place entry to leap to first at the finale in the last five years occurred in 2021. Jan Heylen and Ryan Hardwick won the finale aboard Wright Motorsports’ No. 16 Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 Clubsport RS, which propelled Heylen from 30 points down entering the finale to the championship by 190 points over Turner Motorsport’s Machavern and Bill Auberlen and Machavern, who had a fraught finale en route to 18th in their No. 95 BMW M4 GT4. Subsequent leaders have held leads of 160, 60, 110 and 100 points in GS the last four years and have brought it home. TCR should have no such challenges this year. Mason Filippi and Bryson Morris entered Indianapolis with a 260-point lead in their No. 33 Bryan Herta Autosport Hyundai Elantra N TCR and left it with a 200-point margin over teammates Denis Dupont and Preston Brown in the similar No. 76 Herta Hyundai. That puts them well in line with past champions who entered the finale with 230, 100, 20 and 100-point gaps and then brought it home. Only last year did TCR see a last-race points change. MMG’s No. 93 Honda Civic FL5 TCR of LP Montour and Karl Wittmer had a race fraught with mechanical maladies, opening the door for Harry Gottsacker to overcome a 10-point – or one position – points deficit and claim his second TCR title (2023). Provided Filippi and Morris start the season finale, they’ll score at least last-place points and have enough in hand to wrap the title, which would extend Herta and Hyundai’s run of title form where both team and manufacturer have won six TCR titles in the last seven years. Hyundai has won the last six manufacturer titles (2020 through 2025) and all driver titles since 2019, except 2024. It’d be a first for both drivers, though. title: Drake Surprises Karol G’s Houston Crowd With ‘Ahí,’ ‘Janice STFU’ & ‘One Dance’ Performances - Billboard
content:
The rapper joined the Colombian superstar on stage for three surprise tracks. Drake made a surprise appearance at Karol G‘s concert in Houston on Sunday (Sept. 27), joining the Colombian superstar on stage for three performances. In fan-shot clips from the show, both artists appeared dressed in black, with Drake taking the mic at the ending of Karol performing their collaboration “Ahí,” and reciting his line from the track, “I want a Latina, I want a Latina/ I want a G like Karolina.” He then performed his single “Janice STFU” and his 2016 hit “One Dance” as Karol G danced beside him before the two moved in close, drawing roars from the crowd. The appearance was the latest in a series of moments between the two stars. Drake attended Karol G’s Toronto show in July, appearing on the venue’s Jumbotron, and had publicly nodded to her on record before their team-up, name-checking her on “New Bestie” from his 2026 project MAID OF HONOUR. The pair then released “Ahí” in August, and the single made an immediate mark on Billboard‘s Latin charts. It debuted at No. 1 on Hot Latin Songs — Drake’s fourth leader on the tally — and gave him his first career No. 1 on Hot Latin Rhythm Songs, a chart he had never previously topped. Released in 2016, “One Dance” was a career milestone for Drake. Featuring Nigerian star Wizkid and British singer Kyla, it became his first Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 as a lead artist, spent 10 weeks atop the chart and reigned for years as the most streamed song in Spotify history. It has since become a staple of his unannounced guest spots, including a surprise set at Vybz Kartel’s Toronto concert last year, where he also performed it. For Karol G, the moment adds to a genre-reshaping run. The Medellín-born star became the first Latina to headline Coachella earlier this year, and her 2023 album Mañana Será Bonito made history as the first all-Spanish-language album by a woman to debut at No. 1 on the Billboard 200. Her 2025 album Tropicoqueta debuted at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, and she announced her latest album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, in July, extending a run that has established her as the most commercially dominant woman in Latin music. title: ‘Karol G’s 200 Copas Tequila: Price, Where to Buy and the Story Behind the Bottle’ - ColombiaOne.com
content: Colombian reggaeton star Karol G surprised her fans with the launch of her own tequila brand: 200 Copas, inspired by her hit song of the same name. Over the past two days, the artist had kept her followers in suspense after sharing on her Instagram stories an image of a dark blue glass bottle with the caption: “What started with a song.” Many speculated it was a fragrance inspired by her track Tu perfume. However, Karol G officially confirmed that it was her entry into the spirits industry with 200 Copas by Casa Dragones. True to her reputation for surprising fans, the Colombian artist announced her new project through a video filmed in an agave field, where she spoke about the essence of 200 Copas. In the post, she shared: “Today, after almost three years of working on this, I can finally announce that 200 Copas, our tequila, is a reality.” The announcement sparked a wave of positive reactions on social media, with fans celebrating the launch and saying they can’t wait to toast and sing 200 Copas while enjoying the tequila. The product is an ultra-premium crystalline tequila, crafted from 100% Blue Weber agave. It is aged for more than 12 months in custom-made American oak barrels, resulting in a flavor profile with notes of honey, almond, cooked agave, oak, and citrus. Une publication partagée par 200 Copas by Casa Dragones (@200copasbycasadragones) The 200 Copas packaging was designed as a tribute to the song that inspired it: a bonfire under a midnight blue sky. content: Valkyries news: Why Natalie Nakase credits passionate GS fans before Game 1 vs. Wings appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. As of publication, the Golden State Valkyries were well on their way to a Game 1 win in their opening round playoff series against the Dallas Wings, leading by 30+ points late in the third quarter. And if you listened to the official broadcast, you would hear the unmistakable roar of the Valkyries home crowd. For Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase, as good as the team has been, it's been the fans at 'Ballhalla' that have helped carry them, as per Madisyn Cunningham of Winsidr. "Ballhalla is part of us. They're our Sixth Man. They roar when they're supposed to roar, they're hostile when they're supposed to be hostile … we know we're not going to be able to hear," Nakase said. "Playin here, again, is one of the best. It is literally my dream come true to have this type of energy, because that's how we play. We fight, we punch, we're physical. They're a part of us, they help us with that energy." The Valkyries set home crowd records during their inaugural season last year amid multiple sell-outs. The team made the playoffs in their first seasons as a No. 8 seed, and this year they improved to the No. 2 seed in the league standings. The Valkyries have also been selected as All-Star Weekend host for 2027. This is Natalie Nakase's second season at the helm as Valkyries head coach. She was hired as the franchise's first ever coach after spending three seasons on staff under Becky Hammon with the Las Vegas Aces. She was a part of the Aces' championship teams in 2022 and 2023.
